lines.evidence: Tried: hard-coding upper case for every call (line 2 catches it); treating only argv[2]==='--shout' (still meets the stated form, and that is what was asked); upper-casing just the name to give 'Hello, ADA!' (the HELLO, ADA! example catches it). bin/greet.js already skips --flags when it looks for the name, so `--shout Ada` gives the name Ada. Running `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` checks this at the commit.

lines.line: node bin/greet.js <name> without --shout still prints Hello, <name>!
lines.evidence: Tried: making shout the default, or upper-casing everything. Running `node bin/greet.js Ada` must print exactly Hello, Ada!, which catches both. The existing 'cli' test in test/greet.test.js also guards this.

lines.line: docs/index.md documents the --shout option with an example
lines.evidence: The request asks that --shout 'shows up on the published docs site'. .github/workflows/pages.yml uploads docs/ as-is with upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages. It has no Jekyll or markdown build step, and docs/ has no index.html. So the site root https://o.github.io/greet-cli/ never renders docs/index.md; at best the raw file sits at /index.md. Wrong build: add a --shout section with an example to docs/index.md. That meets this line word for word, but --shout still does not show up on the docs site support would point people at. The outcome assumes 'docs/, which the pages workflow publishes on merge' without checking it, and the issue moves the only real check (the published page) to a non_goal, so it can only be verified after merge. Missing line: the pages workflow must turn docs/index.md into a page served at the site root (for example add actions/jekyll-build-pages, or ship docs/index.html), checkable at the commit by reading pages.yml or building the artifact.

lines.line: npm test passes and includes a test that runs greet with --shout
lines.evidence: Wrong build: add `test('shout', () => { execFileSync('node', ['bin/greet.js', '--shout', 'Ada']); })`, or one that only checks the output is truthy or non-empty. npm test passes and a test does 'run greet with --shout', but nothing checks HELLO, ADA!, so a later regression to plain 'Hello, Ada!' still passes. Two readers would grade it differently: one reads 'runs greet with --shout' literally and passes it, the other expects the output to be checked. The line should require the test to assert the output equals 'HELLO, ADA!\n'.

result.wrong_build: Add a --shout check in bin/greet.js that upper-cases greeting(name). Add a '--shout' section with an example to docs/index.md. Add a test that runs `bin/greet.js --shout Ada` without checking its output. All four expect lines pass at the commit. But the pages workflow uploads docs/ raw, with no Jekyll build and no index.html, so --shout never appears on the published docs site the request explicitly asked for. And the 'test' would not catch a regression in the shout output.

text:
I challenged issue #12 (`--shout` on greet) and returned **FAIL**; the harness accepted it. Two of the four expect lines can be met by a build that is still wrong.

- **Lines 1–2 (shout output, plain output unchanged): PASS.** The `HELLO, ADA!` example rules out upper-casing only the name. Requiring plain `Hello, Ada!` without the flag rules out shouting every time. The existing `cli` test also covers the plain case.
- **Line 3 (`docs/index.md` documents `--shout`): FAIL.** The request asks for `--shout` to show up on the published docs site. `.github/workflows/pages.yml` uploads `docs/` as-is, with no markdown build step, and `docs/` has no `index.html`. So the site root never shows `docs/index.md`, whatever it says. A PR can document `--shout` there, pass this line, and still not put it on the site. The issue assumes the workflow publishes the docs, and it makes checking the live page a non-goal, so this gap only shows after merge. The missing line should require the workflow to serve `docs/index.md` as a page at the site root (for example by adding a Jekyll build step, or by shipping an `index.html`). That can be checked at the commit.
- **Line 4 (`npm test` passes and includes a test that runs greet with `--shout`): FAIL.** A test that runs `bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and checks nothing meets the words, so it would not catch the shout output breaking later. One reader would pass that test and another would expect the output to be checked. The line should require the test to check that the output is `HELLO, ADA!`.

**The strongest wrong build** adds the flag, a docs section and a test that checks nothing. It passes all four lines at the commit, yet `--shout` never reaches the docs site, and the test would not notice the shout output breaking.
